question: What type of tissue makes up the outer layer of the skin, the epidermis?
explanation: The epidermis is made of layered, flat epithelial cells that form a tough outer barrier for the body. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why does the epidermis rely completely on the layer beneath it, the dermis, for survival?

options.A: It lacks the machinery for protein synthesis
options.B: It cannot produce its own structural proteins
options.C: It requires nerve signals from the dermis to grow
options.D: It lacks its own blood supply

explanation: Because blood vessels do not reach the epidermis, nutrients must travel upward from the dermis to feed the cells. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which layer of the epidermis is found only in thick skin, such as the palms of the hands and soles of the feet?
explanation: This clear layer provides extra protection and reduces friction in areas that experience high wear. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h2)

question: In which layer of the epidermis do new skin cells constantly divide to replace older ones?
explanation: Stem cells live in this deepest basal layer, dividing continuously to push older cells toward the surface. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the main protein produced by skin cells that gives skin its strength and toughness?
explanation: Keratin is a tough, fibrous protein that protects underlying tissues from physical and chemical damage. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h3)

question: What happens to skin cells as they travel upward toward the surface of the skin?

options.A: They fill with keratin, lose their cell parts, and die
options.B: They turn into pigment-producing cells called melanocytes
options.C: They multiply rapidly and develop a rich blood supply
options.D: They absorb moisture and become active immune cells

explanation: As cells move upward, they flatten, fill with keratin, and form a protective layer of dead scales. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which cells in the epidermis act as immune guards to catch and fight off foreign invaders?
explanation: Langerhans cells are resident immune cells in the epidermis that alert the body to harmful germs. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which cell type in the deepest layer of the epidermis helps detect light touch by connecting with nerve endings?
explanation: Merkel cells form touch receptors that link up with sensory nerve fibers in the skin. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why do individuals with darker skin tones have more natural protection against ultraviolet (UV) radiation?

options.A: Their melanocytes produce more melanin and larger pigment packages
options.B: Idiopathically, they possess a higher total count of melanocytes
options.C: Their skin cells completely lack nuclei that UV rays can damage
options.D: Their outer skin layer is twice as thick as in lighter skin

explanation: Skin color differences depend on how much melanin is produced and how it is packaged, not the actual number of melanocytes. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the main job of melanin within skin cells?

options.A: Absorbing ultraviolet radiation to protect cell DNA
options.B: Supplying chemical energy for cellular division
options.C: Regulating the local temperature of the skin surface
options.D: Stimulating the immune response against bacterial infections

explanation: Melanin acts as a natural sunscreen by sitting over the control center of skin cells to block harmful UV rays. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h5)

question: How long does it usually take for a new skin cell to travel from the deepest layer to the surface and shed?
explanation: A normal skin renewal cycle takes roughly twenty-eight to thirty days in a healthy adult. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of the continuous shedding of dead cells from the outer surface of the skin?

options.A: It allows sweat glands to empty their contents directly into the air
options.B: It maintains the protective skin barrier and removes trapped surface germs
options.C: It directly generates the body heat needed to warm the blood
options.D: It provides essential nutrients back to the living blood vessels

explanation: Constant shedding clears away surface dirt and bacteria while keeping the tough outer shield fresh. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h6)
